rows.reasoning: His only on-question words call for doing "a better job" on "Section 8 vouchers" and deride a 2026 deregulatory housing bill, which leans away from "Rely on the market to set prices and supply" but names no public housing, no binding rule such as rent caps or required affordable units, and no subsidy to get housing built. Vouchers are demand-side aid, so they do not meet rung 4's "so more affordable housing gets built"; the rungs on the pro-government side stay unseparated.
